No. elephc compiles a subset of PHP and treats unsupported dynamic behaviour as a compile error. Its advice is to keep Laravel or Symfony on regular PHP and compile static, performance-sensitive modules as extensions or libraries.
How is elephc different from the PHP JIT?
The PHP JIT runs inside the Zend Engine and compiles hot code at runtime. elephc compiles ahead of time to a standalone native binary or library with no Zend Engine at all.
Executables for macOS ARM64, Linux ARM64 and Linux x86_64, plus iOS ARM64 device and simulator libraries cross-compiled from macOS.
Can I write a PHP extension with elephc?
Yes. elephc --emit phpext builds a .so module that a standard PHP 8.5 install can load, so you can write an extension in PHP instead of C.
